title: Fourier inversion and first coordinate rule on Schwartz tests
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] and Lebesgue measure on Euclidean $\mathbf R^m$, where $m\geq1$. Write $\mathcal S$ for the complex Schwartz class: smooth functions $\psi$ such that $\sup_x\|x\|^k\|D^n\psi(x)\|<\infty$ for every pair of integers $k,n\geq0$. Define $\mathcal F\psi(\xi)=\int e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\psi(x)\,dx$ and $\mathcal G\psi(\xi)=\int e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\psi(x)\,dx$. Both $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ are complex-linear maps from $\mathcal S$ to $\mathcal S$, with $\mathcal G\mathcal F\psi=\psi$ and $\mathcal F\mathcal G\psi=\psi$. For every coordinate $j$, $$\partial_{x_j}(\mathcal F\psi)(x)=\mathcal F\bigl(\xi\mapsto-2\pi i\xi_j\psi(\xi)\bigr)(x).$$
